correctness.rationale: The contraction identity counts exactly B_{c(F)}. Distinguishing whether F contains the unique triangle yields the two exact sectors. Poisson size-bias proves the forest-sector positivity; the cubic Q moment and strict rational Dobinski bound prove V_{s,s}>0 for every s>=6, the V recurrence and exact s=7 base prove all s>=7 rows positive, and direct exact rows s<=6 determine negative inertia. The cross-sector difference is 2U_{s+2,s}>0, giving the exact global sharp minimum. Standalone verification enumerated 3<=n<=9 all set partitions for two graph topologies and passed 34286 exact comparisons plus arithmetic recurrence tests through n=180. Finite checks are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: Triangle-unicyclic graphs are the first topologically nonforest connected class, introducing a minimal cycle dependency into the known co-block projection model. Determining whether all frequencies survive, when the natural symmetric convolution becomes positive definite, the full exceptional negative dimensions, and the unique extremal frequency/condition number are motivated structural spectral recovery questions; the exact n=10 phase transition is nonmonotone at small sizes and does not follow from mean counts or positivity of ordinary Bell numbers. The classification works uniformly over arbitrary tree attachments, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
